answer: Weight jury selection by earned history: instead of picking graders at random, the network selects jurors in proportion to their verified record of honest work over past epochs. A willow that bends with every wind — a fresh identity with no record — is never chosen, so a Sybil army cannot capture the jury. A ferrous-strong history takes epochs to build, and each juror's past grades are public, so a bad actor is visible before it is picked. Honesty with a copper-bottomed record earns selection; a thousand new fakes, however many, hold zero weight in the draw.
